In summary, VirG-directed antibodies exhibited robust antimicrobial activity and mediated cross-serotype protection. These findings support VirG as a promising component of next-generation protein-based Shigella vaccines.

title: A staged clinical development and evidence-generation framework for Group A Streptococcus vaccines
abstract: Group A Streptococcus (Strep A) causes substantial global morbidity and mortality, yet vaccine development faces scientific, regulatory, and strategic challenges. We propose a platform-agnostic, staged clinical development and evidence-generation framework aligning trial feasibility with public health priorities. Laboratory-confirmed symptomatic pharyngitis could provide a feasible pivotal efficacy endpoint for initial licensure, subject to regulatory agreement. Complementary efficacy, effectiveness, and implementation studies could then generate evidence across diverse populations and outcomes.

title: Intranasal vaccination with pneumococcal protein antigens presented on Salmonella outer membrane vesicles confers broad, serotype-independent protection
authors: H. Bart van den Berg van Saparoea
Christa E. van der Gaast- de Jongh
abstract: Despite widespread vaccination, an unmet need remains for a broadly protective pneumococcal vaccine preventing colonisation and transmission, critical precursors of disease and spread. An intranasal, protein-based vaccine with intrinsic adjuvant activity may represent a promising alternative to pneumococcal conjugate vaccines (PCVs). We developed an antigen delivery platform based on Salmonella -derived outer membrane vesicles (OMVs) engineered for SpyCatcher-SpyTag-mediated covalent coupling of heterologous antigens, thereby combining modular antigen display with intrinsic adjuvant activity. OMVs displaying pneumococcal antigens AliA and PnrA (OMV-A-P) were produced under GLP conditions, characterised and evaluated in toxicology and potency studies in mice and rats. Intranasal administration of OMV-A-P was well-tolerated and elicited robust systemic and mucosal antibody responses capable of recognising a broad range of pneumococcal strains. Vaccination also induced local and systemic pneumococcal-specific IL-17 recall responses, supporting its potential as a serotype-independent vaccine candidate. Protection against pneumococcal colonisation was demonstrated for two distinct clinical strains and persisted for at least 15 weeks after the third vaccination. Notably, in animals previously vaccinated with PCV, OMV-A-P remained immunogenic and conferred superior protection against pneumococcal colonisation compared to PCV-only vaccinated mice. Collectively, this indicates that OMV-A-P is a promising next-generation intranasal pneumococcal vaccine candidate warranting development towards a first-in-human study.

title: A structure-guided trivalent subunit vaccine confers maternal protection to neonatal piglets against PEDV and PDCoV
abstract: Antigenic divergence among porcine epidemic diarrhea virus (PEDV) genotypes and porcine deltacoronavirus (PDCoV) limits the cross-protection provided by current commercial vaccines. Here, employing a structure-guided antigen design strategy, we developed a trivalent subunit vaccine concurrently targeting PEDV G2a, PEDV G2b, and PDCoV. The vaccine antigen set comprises optimized spike ectodomain antigens, featuring stabilizing mutations, a heptad repeat 2 (HR2) deletion, a fused neutralizing epitope, and a flagellin adjuvant fused to the N-terminus. Formulated with MF59+CpG adjuvants, this trivalent vaccine elicited robust PEDV- and PDCoV-specific neutralizing antibody responses and Th1/Th2-associated cellular immune responses characterized by IFN-γ, IL-2, and IL-4 production in mice. Immunization of pregnant sows with 300 μg dose induced high-titer IgG, IgA, and colostral secretory IgA (SIgA) against all three target viruses. Although neutralizing antibody titers were comparable between the 100 μg and 300 μg dose groups, the 300 μg group showed higher and more persistent levels of colostral binding IgG and SIgA. Following maternal immunization, piglets that acquired maternal antibodies through colostrum exhibited reduced clinical diarrhea, lower fecal viral RNA shedding, and less severe intestinal lesions after challenge with PEDV G2a, PEDV G2b, or PDCoV. These findings support this structure-guided trivalent subunit vaccine as a promising candidate for maternal immunization against co-circulating porcine enteric coronaviruses.

title: Genome-wide association study of conjugated pneumococcal vaccine antibody responses in South African infants
authors: Fiona R. M. van der Klis
abstract: Pneumococcal conjugate vaccines have substantially reduced global mortality, yet the genetic basis of vaccine-induced immunity is unclear. We analysed host genetic determinants of PCV7-induced IgG responses in 1017 South African infants. No genome-wide significant associations were identified, including at the HLA locus. In contrast to protein vaccines, where HLA strongly shapes responses, PCV7 responses appear less constrained by HLA-mediated antigen presentation. This reduced constraint could partially explain their consistent effectiveness across diverse populations.

title: Immunogenicity and protective efficacy of a recombinant HtsA-SLOdm fusion protein against Group A Streptococcus infection
abstract: Group A Streptococcus (GAS) is a major human pathogen responsible for a broad spectrum of diseases, yet no licensed vaccine is currently available. Heme-transfer lipoprotein A (HtsA) and streptolysin O (SLO) are key virulence-associated factors involved in iron acquisition and host cell damage, respectively, making them attractive vaccine targets. Here, we designed and evaluated HtsA-SLOdm, a recombinant fusion protein comprising HtsA and a detoxified mutant of SLO, to assess its immunogenicity and protective efficacy against GAS infection. The fusion protein retained the antigenicity of both components and exhibited negligible hemolytic activity without detectable histopathological toxicity in immunized mice. Immunization with alum-adjuvanted HtsA-SLOdm elicited robust antigen-specific antibody responses, with endpoint IgG titers ranging from 1:312,500 to 1:1,562,500. In a murine skin infection model, HtsA-SLOdm vaccination improved survival, reduced lesion size and bacterial load, and alleviated tissue damage, accompanied by enhanced collagen deposition and angiogenesis. Antisera from immunized mice also mediated opsonophagocytic killing of GAS. Mechanistically, HtsA-SLOdm promoted dendritic cell maturation, B-cell activation, and Th1, Th2, and Th17-associated cytokine responses. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that HtsA-SLOdm induces robust humoral and cellular immunity and confers significant protection against GAS infection, highlighting its potential as a promising candidate for GAS vaccine development.

title: Maternal immunization with RSV-VLPs in a non-human primate model of RSV infection
abstract: Using a non-human primate model, we evaluated an RSV pre-fusion F and G protein virus-like particle-based maternal immunization strategy and evaluated the effects of pregnancy on vaccine-induced immunity against RSV. Immunization during pregnancy induced robust systemic and mucosal IgG and neutralizing antibody titers. Upon post-partum challenge, this vaccination strategy enhanced humoral recall responses and Fc-effector functions, and reduced viral load in dams. Infants born to vaccinated dams had increased levels of RSV antibodies in the plasma and lung mucosa, which were correlated with reduced viral load; these infants also exhibited reduced pulmonary eosinophilia. Interestingly, vaccination during pregnancy was associated with increased post-fusion F responses and NAb titers, and we observed a reduction in viral load following post-partum challenge compared to nonpregnant controls. These results support the potential of a VLP-based maternal immunization strategy and provide insight into vaccine-induced immunity against RSV in pregnant and post-partum adults and infants.

title: Cross-protection of wildtype and vaccine-derived chikungunya virus antibodies against chikungunya and Mayaro viruses in mice
abstract: The live-attenuated vaccine IXCHIQ against chikungunya virus (CHIKV) was approved in 2023, with its efficacy evaluated using human neutralizing antibody titers as surrogate effectiveness criterion. Previous in vivo studies assessed its efficacy at high CHIKV-specific antibody titers, whereas its efficacy and antibody-dependent enhancement (ADE) risks at suboptimal levels mimicking long-term immunity remain poorly characterized. Here, we assessed antibody-mediated protection following vaccination or natural infection by passively immunizing transiently immunocompromised mice with graded doses of pooled immune sera before challenge with two CHIKV genotypes or the related Mayaro virus (MAYV). Protection was evaluated using viral loads at 3 days post-infection and clinical parameters. Vaccine- and infection-induced antibodies conferred strong protection against both CHIKV genotypes, even at antibody concentrations nearing ELISA detection limits. In contrast, protection against MAYV required higher titers. We observed no ADE. Our findings align with previous studies supporting durable protection against CHIKV and partial cross-protection against MAYV.

title: Rational engineering of Omp34 loop-based immunogen enhances protection against Colistin-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii
abstract: The surface antigens are promising immunogenic targets for vaccine development and immunotherapies. Here, the loop3 to loop7 (L3-L7) region of the Omp34 from Acinetobacter baumannii was evaluated. A DNA fragment encoding the L3-L7 region was amplified from the Omp34 gene. The structures of ΔL5/5Gly-L3-L7 and ΔL5/Acr-L3-L7 were achieved through the modification of the loop 5 sequence in the L3-L7 of Omp34. Optimization of Omp34 loop epitopes via Acr sequence linkage was performed. Omp34, L3-L7 region, ΔL5/5Gly-L3-L7 and ΔL5/Acr-L3-L7 were recombinantly expressed. Mice immunized with the purified antigens, were infected with the clinical isolate of A. baumannii 58ST. Active immunizations with ΔL5/Acr-L3-L7, L3-L7, Omp34 and ΔL5/5Gly-L3-L7 resulted in 75%, 50%, 37.5% and 37.5% survival rates, respectively. Passive immunization with sera from these antigens in the same order results in survival rates of 62.5%, 37.5%, 25% and 25%, respectively. Anti-ΔL5/Acr-L3-L7 sera mediated the greatest opsonophagocytic killing activity. In addition, active and passive immunizations with ΔL5/Acr-L3-L7 resulted in the highest bacterial clearance in the lung, spleen, and liver. These findings suggest that the L3-L7 region of Omp34 is an appropriate scaffold and antigen against A. baumannii , in which replacing loop 5 with the Acr sequence could enhance its antigenicity and protectivity.

title: Preparation quality and epitranscriptomic modification influence circular RNA vaccine performance
abstract: Circular RNA (circRNA) is an emerging vaccine modality that is proposed to improve stability, reduce reactogenicity and extend antigen expression compared with linear mRNA. However, the relative contributions to vaccine performance of its covalently closed structure, its preparation quality and nucleotide modifications remain poorly described. Here, we systematically dissected these parameters in vivo across two antigen systems. We identified RNA preparation quality as a major contributor to markers of circRNA reactogenicity, with innate immune activation tracking with the abundance of residual low molecular weight RNA species in less refined preparations. High-quality circRNA exhibited markedly reduced innate immune activation compared with linear mRNA, independent of nucleotide modification. Despite these differences, circRNA and mRNA vaccines elicited comparable antibody titres and T cell responses, indicating that reduced innate activation did not translate into enhanced adaptive immune magnitude. Incorporating N 6 -methyladenosine (m 6 A) did not affect markers of reactogenicity or antigen expression but was associated with increased antibody avidity across both antigen systems, with neutralisation trending in the same direction. CircRNA vaccination also altered the anatomical distribution of germinal centre responses, reducing splenic antigen-specific germinal centre B cells at the measured timepoint while preserving lymph node responses. Together, these findings indicate that circRNA vaccine performance is shaped by RNA preparation quality and epitranscriptomic modification, rather than differences in innate immune activation.

title: Coordinated serum interferon gamma and IL-15 responses to PfRAS vaccination are associated with protection from malaria
abstract: Immunization with radiation-attenuated sporozoites (PfRAS) is highly protective against Plasmodium falciparum malaria, but our understanding of protective correlates is incomplete. The IMRAS study used a PfRAS dose aimed at 50% efficacy to enable discovery of protective correlates. We performed serum proteomics, assaying 2925 serum proteins at five IMRAS study timepoints for 6 protected and 5 non-protected donors, to identify secreted proteins that correlate with immunization and/or protection. We next integrated this serum proteomics dataset with whole blood transcriptomic responses and proportions of circulating immune cells to identify involved signaling pathways and cell subsets. We identified 21 vaccine-induced proteins, including IFNG and IL15. IFNG-stimulated PBMCs from protected IMRAS participants showed increased CXCL9 and CXCL10 responses vs. non-protected participants. IFNG levels in protected individuals correlated with IL15, as well as interferon response gene expression levels in whole blood, and circulating activated CD14+ monocytes. Altogether, this analysis showed that PfRAS can prevent blood-stage malaria infection via coordinated IFNG and IL15 production, activation of CD14+ monocytes, and subsequent production of CXCL9, CXCL10, and CXCL11.

title: Linear cap-independent mRNA vaccines as an emerging vaccine platform
abstract: Linear cap-independent mRNA (LciRNA) is an emerging vaccine platform enabling cap-independent translation while retaining a linear RNA architecture. This review summarizes LciRNA design principles, including IRES-mediated initiation, stability engineering, and immune regulation, and compares LciRNA with major mRNA vaccine platforms. We discuss current preclinical progress, particularly in cancer vaccines, and analyze challenges in potency, manufacturability, application scope, and clinical translation.

title: SARS-CoV-2 breakthrough infections imprint signatures of enhanced immunity against COVID-19
abstract: SARS-CoV-2-specific immunity has been shaped in recent years by a combination of natural infection, complicated by ongoing viral evolution, and vaccination. However, it has remained unclear to what extent combined antigen challenge, which elicits so-called hybrid immunity, impacts clinical outcomes and subsequent protection against COVID-19. In this study, we evaluated spike-specific humoral and cellular immune responses elicited by hybrid antigen exposure versus vaccination alone, considering the order of challenge and disease severity after infection with SARS-CoV-2. Hybrid antigen exposure was characterized by enhanced humoral and cellular immune responses compared with vaccination alone. CD8 + T cell responses were also more cross-reactive and displayed skewed epitope targeting hierarchies in the context of hybrid immunity. These features were maintained in older adults, who typically exhibit age-related deficits in de novo immunity, especially after breakthrough infections (BTIs). BTIs were further associated with more coordinated adaptive immune responses compared with those elicited by vaccination after infection with SARS-CoV-2. We also found that humoral immune responses, specifically IgG antibody titers targeting the spike protein receptor-binding domain, were better maintained after mRNA vaccination and that cellular immune responses were better maintained after vectored vaccination in the wake of BTIs. Moreover, vaccination was associated with mild disease after subsequent infection, especially among individuals who had received a booster dose. These results suggest that vaccine-induced memory responses, which generally wane over time, can be reactivated and reshaped by BTIs, amplifying features associated with enhanced immunity against SARS-CoV-2.

title: RTS,S-induced off-target antibody responses in malaria-naïve adults associated with protection against controlled human malaria infection
abstract: RTS,S, a WHO-recommended malaria vaccine, targets the circumsporozoite protein (CSP) on the Plasmodium falciparum sporozoite surface. Emerging data suggest off-target (non-CSP) antibody responses are associated with RTS,S-induced protection, but vaccine-derived responses are challenging to differentiate from boosting of naturally acquired immunity in endemic areas. We probed pre-challenge sera from RTS,S-vaccinated malaria-naïve adults who were either protected ( n = 18) or unprotected ( n = 17) against controlled human malaria infection on a custom peptide array with 1747 total variants from 130 non-CSP proteins from across the parasite lifecycle to assess off-target antibody responses with amino acid-level precision. Compared with the unprotected group, the protected group had increased IgG and/or IgA responses to 124 proteins (95%) studied. Using ssearch36, we found that 22 protein regions associated with protection had sequence similarities to CSP epitopes, including regions not found in RTS,S. The finding that off-target antibody responses are induced by RTS,S and are associated with protection in this and other studies suggests that they could be a marker of improved avidity, improved effector functions, or could be mediating improved protection by binding CSP or other proteins. Differentially reactive epitopes without linear sequence homology with CSP could represent conformational epitopes. Further study of these off-target antibody responses could help identify improved strategies for next-generation malaria vaccines.

title: Stakeholder-informed use cases and target product characteristics for vaccines and therapeutics for Nipah virus disease
authors: On behalf of the Nipah Countermeasure Use Case Working Group
abstract: Nipah virus (NiV) is a deadly zoonotic pathogen with potential for severe outbreaks. We convened a multi-stakeholder expert consultation to define potential implementation strategies and use cases for NiV countermeasures across hypothetical outbreak scenarios and conditions. Participants identified distinct roles for vaccines, monoclonal antibodies (mAbs), and small-molecule therapeutics (SMTs) for prevention, post-exposure protection, and treatment. These stakeholder-informed outputs are intended to inform product development, target product profiles, and equitable access during future outbreaks.
